issues.legal_issue: A foster son may be a member of a landlord’s family for a personal-need eviction claim when the circumstances show that he was brought up and treated as the landlord’s own son.
material_facts: The landlord and her husband brought up the husband’s brother’s son as their son, and he lived with them.
He acted as a devoted son and assisted the husband in his business.

The husband’s will recorded that he had brought up the foster son, provided for the business to be carried on by the landlord and the foster son, and gave the foster son’s children the remainder in the residential house after the landlord’s life interest.
The landlord sought eviction of a tenant from a non-residential building for the business needs of herself and the foster son.
issues.conclusion: The foster son was a member of the landlord’s family in the circumstances of the case, so the landlord’s personal-need eviction application could be based on his need as well as her own. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(6A) of the Tamil Nadu Buildings (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1960 defines a landlord’s family by listing a spouse, son, daughter, grandchild or dependent parent, but the opening words of Section 2 make those definitions subject to a contrary contextual requirement. A definition must be read in the context and scheme of the Act and in a way that advances, rather than defeats, its purpose. The meaning of “family” is flexible, and “son” is not invariably confined to a natural son. Applying K. Balakrishna Rao & Ors. v. Haji Abdulla Sait & Ors. and Corporation of the City of Nagpur v. Nagpur Handloom Cloth Market Co. Ltd., and the authorities recognizing that family can include persons not related by blood, the Court held that a child brought up from infancy as one’s own, with parental care and treatment, may be a family member, particularly when held out as one’s own. Whether a foster child qualifies depends on the facts and circumstances; it does not follow that every foster child is a family member.

rule.if: rent_control_personal_need_eviction and foster_child and raised_from_infancy_as_own and received_parental_care and held_out_as_own

predicates.rent_control_personal_need_eviction: A landlord sought a tenant’s eviction under rent-control law on the ground of the landlord’s personal need.
predicates.foster_child: The person whose need supported the eviction claim was not the landlord’s natural child but was brought up by the landlord as a child.
predicates.raised_from_infancy_as_own: The landlord brought the child up from infancy as the landlord’s own child.
predicates.received_parental_care: The child received the love, care, upbringing and support that a parent would provide to a child.
predicates.held_out_as_own: The landlord presented or treated the child as the landlord’s own son.
predicates.foster_child_is_family_member_for_person: The foster child is treated as a member of the landlord’s family for the personal-need eviction claim.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks eviction for personal need and has brought up a foster child from infancy with parental care while treating the child as their own, the child counts as a family member for that claim.
